mainTopic: When a guarantor (עָרֵב) needs a קנין to be obligated, and the closing of מסכת בבא בתרא
overview: This last amud of מסכת בבא בתרא finishes the discussion of when a guarantor (ערב) becomes legally bound. First, the גמרא draws an inference from an earlier ruling. Only a guarantor who commits in front of a בית דין is bound without a קנין, so an ordinary guarantor needs a קנין. Then the גמרא gives the final הלכה. A guarantor who commits when the loan money is handed over needs no קנין. One who commits after the money was already given needs a קנין. A guarantor in front of a בית דין needs no קנין, because he enjoys being trusted by the court and so truly commits. The amud ends with the הדרן closing פרק גט פשוט and the whole מסכת.

steps.title: Only a court guarantor is exempt from needing a kinyan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the previous case narrowly. A ערב who commits in front of a בית דין needs no קנין, but an ordinary ערב does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only a guarantor in front of a court who does not need a kinyan. This shows that a guarantor in an ordinary setting does need a kinyan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the earlier case to a guarantor who committed in front of a בית דין. That way it cannot be used to prove that every guarantor is bound without a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case seemed to show that a ערב is bound without a קנין. This line says that case was special because the guarantee was made in front of a בית דין. So the general rule stays in place: an ordinary ערב needs a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor who promises to pay if the borrower does not
A formal act that makes a commitment legally binding
A guarantor who takes on the guarantee in front of a court
In general; in an ordinary situation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a ערב is never bound without a קנין. The very next step shows another case, committing at the time the money is given, where no קנין is needed either.

phrases.english: It is a guarantor of the court
phrases.notes: He means a guarantor who took on the guarantee in front of the judges.

phrases.english: who does not require a kinyan,
but generally, he requires a kinyan.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָרֵב דְּבֵית דִּין הוּא דְּלָא בָּעֵי קִנְיָן, הָא בְּעָלְמָא בָּעֵי קִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the guarantor by limiting the case that came before this text.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the court-guarantor case as proof that every guarantor is bound without a קנין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case was special because it was in front of a בית דין, so it does not show the general rule.

steps.title: The final הלכה on when a guarantor needs a קנין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules on three cases. A ערב at the time the money is given needs no קנין. A ערב after the money was given needs a קנין. A ערב in front of a בית דין needs no קנין, because he enjoys being trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a guarantor who commits when the money is handed over does not need a קנין. One who commits after the money was handed over does need a קנין. A guarantor in front of a court does not need a קנין. Because he enjoys the fact that the court trusts him, he makes up his mind to bind himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical הלכה about when a guarantor is bound. It also explains why a guarantor in front of a בית דין is bound even after the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of the loan, the lender hands over money because of the guarantor's promise, so the guarantor is bound without a קנין. After the loan, the lender gave nothing in return for the promise, so a קנין is needed. In front of a בית דין, the guarantor is pleased that the court relies on him. That pleasure is what makes him truly commit.

keyTerms.meaning: The handing over of the loan money
He fully decides and binds himself

steps.whatToRemember: A guarantor at the time of the loan needs no קנין. A guarantor after the loan needs a קנין. A guarantor in front of a בית דין needs no קנין, because being trusted by the court makes him fully commit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה about guarantors that is followed in monetary law. It shows that a person can become bound by what he receives in return, whether money given because of his promise or the satisfaction of being trusted.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: a guarantor at the time the money is given
after the money is given, he requires a kinyan.

phrases.aramaic: עָרֵב דְּבֵית דִּין – לָא בָּעֵי קִנְיָן;
phrases.english: A guarantor in front of the court does not require a kinyan;
because for that satisfaction, that he is trusted,
phrases.notes: The trust here is the court relying on him.

phrases.english: he fully decides and binds himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1 and gives the full final ruling, adding the case of a guarantor at the time the money is given.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ערב at the time of the loan needs no קנין, after the loan needs a קנין, and in front of a בית דין needs no קנין because being trusted makes him commit.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק גט פשוט and מסכת בבא בתרא
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק גט פשוט, which is also the end of all of מסכת בבא בתרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, גט פשוט, and מסכת בבא בתרא is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק, and here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'הדרן עלך' we promise to come back and learn this פרק again. Since גט פשוט is the last פרק, the line adds that מסכת בבא בתרא is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing line said at the end of a chapter
A plain (unfolded) document; the name of the last chapter of בבא בתרא

phrases.english: We will return to you, Get Pashut,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the tractate after the final הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק גט פשוט and מסכת בבא בתרא are complete.
